title: Exact uniform spanning-tree sampling in linear time
formal: Is there a uniform randomized word-RAM algorithm that, on every connected simple unweighted undirected graph G with m edges, outputs an exactly uniform spanning tree in expected \(O(m)\) total time?
definitions:
The graph has n≥1 labelled vertices and is supplied by adjacency lists with every undirected edge represented at both endpoints. For n=1 the algorithm returns the empty tree in O(1) time; the asymptotic bound is O(m+1). A spanning tree is an acyclic connected subset of n−1 input edges. Let T(G) be the finite set of all such subsets. Exact uniformity means that for every H∈T(G), the output probability equals 1/|T(G)|.

Use a word-RAM with word size Theta(log(n+2)), large enough for graph addresses, and unit-cost arithmetic, comparisons, shifts, bit operations, reads, writes and fresh independent uniform random words. Unbounded exact real arithmetic is unavailable. The algorithm terminates almost surely, always returns a valid spanning tree, and has expected cost at most C(m+1) on each fixed input, for one absolute C. Reading or transforming the graph, preprocessing, random-number generation and writing all tree edges are charged. Rejection sampling is allowed and its work is counted. There is no total-variation tolerance, failure symbol or conditioning on successful runs in the output specification. Weighted graphs are outside this card’s target.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked sampler with proofs of exact uniformity, almost-sure termination and the expected linear bound, or a complete impossibility proof in this model. An almost-linear m^(1+o(1)) runtime is insufficient. A distribution within small total variation distance is also insufficient, even if its computational bound is linear.
context: Schild gives an almost-linear exact sampling result, including for unweighted graphs, and separately analyzes approximate sampling. The distinction matters because this card requires exact probabilities.
why: This asks whether exact random generation can match the cost of reading the graph.

import_provenance.original_title: Exact uniform spanning-tree sampling in linear time
import_provenance.original_statement: Can an exactly uniform random spanning tree of any connected unweighted undirected graph be generated in expected O(m) time in the standard word-RAM model? Broder’s random-walk sampler launched this line of work, and subsequent almost-linear algorithms do not attain the literal linear-time target.
